docs.text: PySTAC extension generator ¶ pystac-ext-generator is a generic Python command-line application that turns a STAC Extension JSON Schema into a standalone Python module containing PySTAC-compatible extension classes . The input schema determines the class name, registration URI, fields, types, and applicable STAC objects. Declared nested objects become additional value classes; Collection summary helpers are generated when the schema exposes summary fields. The generator is not tied to a particular extension or scientific domain. pystac-ext-generator schema.json -o extension.py Import the generated class from extension.py and use its ext() method to wrap a PySTAC object. The generated module runs independently of the generator. Embedded offline schema validation is available with --include-validation . Start here ¶ Install the CLI . Generate and use your first extension . Work with generated fields and nested classes . Bundle external references . Look up CLI options or the Python API . Understand schema discovery and validation . Python 3.10 or later is required. Lean modules such as Themes need only PySTAC. Embedded validation and schema-dependent union decoding additionally need jsonschema; wide factories use typing-extensions. Generated code never requires Click, Jinja2, Ruff, or pystac-ext-generator .

docs.text: Explanation ¶ Architecture and validation explains how schema discovery, class generation, and runtime wrappers fit together, what validation guarantees, and which JSON Schema constructs require care.
docs.title: Overview

docs.text: Architecture and validation explains how schema discovery, class generation, and runtime wrappers fit together, what validation guarantees, and which JSON Schema constructs require care.
docs.title: Explanation

docs.text: Architecture and validation ¶ From schema to source ¶ The generator reads a full STAC Extension JSON Schema and follows references from STAC object locations. Item metadata lives under properties ; Collection and Catalog metadata lives at the top level. Assets, item asset definitions, Links, and Collection summaries are discovered through their respective containers. Root type constraints restrict applicable branches. Unused definitions are not turned into extension fields just because they exist. The title supplies the extension class name, and $id supplies the registration URI. Field names and constraints come from the schema, with no separate class, URI, field-pointer, or target overrides. The package separates these responsibilities: Component Responsibility cli.py Load inputs, handle options, report diagnostics, and write output. bundle.py Copy and embed explicitly supplied or fetched external resources. schema.py Resolve local pointers and discover fields and STAC targets. models.py Build internal rendering metadata for nested classes and conversion plans. generator.py Validate the schema, render templates, and check output syntax. Jinja2 templates Emit the standalone extension and nested value classes. Change the input schema and regenerate to change an extension contract. Generated files are artifacts; manual edits will be lost during regeneration. Runtime integration ¶ A generated extension wraps an existing PySTAC object and writes its normal metadata dictionaries. PySTAC handles serialization through to_dict() and from_dict() . Nested generated values encode as plain JSON objects and arrays. Call the generated class's ext() method directly. Generation does not install into pystac.extensions , register an item.ext accessor, or provide migration hooks. Extension membership checks the exact canonical schema version. Lean output contains PySTAC wrappers and only the required conversion helpers. Themes needs no jsonschema dependency or embedded schema. --include-validation adds an offline extension validator. Nested object unions also embed the schema and use jsonschema when matching a representation requires validation. Wide factory signatures use typing-extensions. The generator, Ruff, and the template engine are not dependencies of emitted modules. Validation boundaries ¶ Generation validates the schema itself, parses the generated Python source, normalizes imports, and formats it with Ruff. It does not execute the emitted module or validate future data values. At runtime, property annotations describe expected values. Setters and apply() do not enforce every schema constraint. apply() checks all field names and targets before mutation, then assigns values; it is not a general transactional update if serialization of a later value fails. Nested factories enforce the presence of unconditional required arguments. By default, use PySTAC's item.validate() or the equivalent owning-object method for schema validation. This uses PySTAC's normal registered-schema resolver. When generated with --include-validation , extension.validate() checks the complete object against the embedded extension schema, including bounds, formats, and conditional constraints, without retrieving the extension schema. For Assets, Links, and ItemAssetDefinitions, validation uses the owning STAC object and requires an owner. Serialization alone does not validate metadata. The optional embedded validator checks the extension schema, not STAC core. PySTAC's object-level validate() also covers core validation; its schema resolution and network behavior are separate from the embedded validator. Limitations ¶ Conditional applicability is approximated and produces a generation warning. Accessor availability does not establish that every combination is schema-valid. Standalone field-definition fragments do not identify STAC targets. Supply the complete extension schema and reference fields from their intended locations. Unprefixed STAC core/common metadata names are reserved during field discovery. Declared extension fields outside that set, such as renders , are supported. Recursive records are supported. Recursive non-object values can use Any at recursion boundaries and produce warnings; complex intersections can also have conservative annotations without losing validation constraints. Ambiguous nested object unions raise an error when no unique representation can be selected. Inspect raw properties or fix the data before decoding again. Heterogeneous pattern-property maps and tuple arrays remain raw JSON values with warnings. Dynamic property names do not become named accessors. Nested $id scopes, named anchors, $dynamicRef , $recursiveRef , and mixed schema dialects in bundles are rejected. Domain-specific calculations, migrations, and custom semantic helpers are not generated. Nested Band records can be modeled, but Band-level attachment helpers are not generated. Use --strict when generation warnings should stop your build. Keep schema sources under version control and review regenerated modules alongside schema changes.

docs.text: Install and build ¶ Install from a checkout ¶ Use Python 3.10 or later: git clone https://github.com/Terradue/pystac-ext-generator.git cd pystac-ext-generator python -m pip install -e . pystac-ext-generator --help pystac-ext-generator --version The distribution is pystac-ext-generator ; its Python import package is pystac_ext_generator . Installation provides the pystac-ext-generator command. You can also invoke it with python -m pystac_ext_generator . With uv, run uv sync , then uv run pystac-ext-generator --help . If an editable installation predates a packaging change, repeat the installation. Use generated modules in another project ¶ Copy the generated .py module into your application or package and install its runtime dependencies: python -m pip install "pystac>=1.12,<2" Also install jsonschema>=4.23,<5 if you enable embedded validation or the module uses schema-based nested union decoding. Large nested factories use typing-extensions>=4.12,<5 for typed keyword arguments. Ruff is a generation-time dependency only. Import classes from the generated module's name. For example, quality_extension.py provides from quality_extension import QualityExtension when the schema title is Quality Extension . Generation does not install a module into pystac.extensions or register a global PySTAC accessor. Preview the documentation ¶ From the repository checkout, install the documentation tools: python -m pip install "mkdocs<2" "mkdocstrings[python]" pymdown-extensions mkdocs serve -f mkdocs.yaml Build with warnings treated as errors: mkdocs build --strict -f mkdocs.yaml The configuration uses MkDocs' built-in Read the Docs theme. API pages read the source package from src . Run repository checks ¶ With Hatch installed, run: hatch run dev:format-check hatch run dev:lint-check hatch run dev:typecheck hatch run dev:security hatch run test:test The test matrix covers Python 3.10–3.14. Tests generate modules from local schema fixtures and exercise them with real PySTAC objects.

docs.text: Load schemas and bundle references ¶ Choose an input source ¶ The positional SCHEMA argument accepts a UTF-8 JSON file, an HTTP(S) URL, or - for stdin: pystac-ext-generator schema.json -o extension.py pystac-ext-generator https://stac-extensions.github.io/view/v1.1.0/schema.json -o view_extension.py cat schema.json | pystac-ext-generator - > extension.py The schema must have a usable title and an absolute HTTP(S) $id , regardless of its input location. Diagnostics go to stderr and generated source goes to stdout unless --output is supplied. Use trusted schema sources. Resolve external documents offline ¶ Local JSON Pointers such as #/$defs/fields work automatically. References to other documents need explicit resource mappings or opt-in fetching. pystac-ext-generator schema.json \ --reference 'https://example.org/common/schema.json=common-schema.json' \ -o extension.py Repeat --reference URI=FILE for every external resource needed. The URI must match the resource's resolved absolute URL. Relative references resolve against the root schema's canonical $id , not its local filename. Fetch external documents ¶ pystac-ext-generator \ https://stac-extensions.github.io/storage/v2.0.0/schema.json \ --resolve-external -o storage_extension.py --resolve-external permits HTTP(S) requests for missing external resources. It can be combined with offline mappings; mapped resources are used first. Each HTTP operation has a 30-second timeout. Bundling accepts at most 100 external documents and requires compatible schema dialects. Bundling embeds the external documents and rewrites their references into local JSON Pointers. Add --include-validation to emit an offline extension validator using the bundled schema. Without that flag, normal full-object validation stays with PySTAC and its schema resolver; nested union decoding embeds the schema only when it needs it. The root $id remains the registration identifier. Regenerate reproducibly ¶ Keep the source schema and referenced files under version control, use offline mappings, and regenerate with --force after reviewing schema changes. --strict turns generation warnings into errors, useful when approximate conditional applicability or conservative annotations are unacceptable for your workflow.
docs.title: Bundle external references

docs.text: Use generated extension classes ¶ The first examples continue from the item and extension created in the tutorial , which enables --include-validation . For default lean output, use the owning STAC object's validate() through PySTAC. Update or remove fields ¶ extension . apply ( score = 0.8 ) assert extension . details . method == "manual" # Omitted fields are preserved. extension . details = None assert "quality:details" not in item . properties extension . clear ( "score" ) assert "quality:score" not in item . properties extension . score = 0.9 apply() uses generated Python attribute names and updates only supplied fields. Unknown or inapplicable names are rejected before any update. Assigning None or calling clear() removes a field. To store explicit JSON null, use set_null("score") ; the tutorial schema does not allow null for score, so subsequent validation would reject it. Attach asset metadata ¶ asset = pystac . Asset ( "https://example.org/image.tif" , media_type = "image/tiff" ) item . add_asset ( "image" , asset ) asset_extension = QualityExtension . ext ( asset ) assert asset_extension . score == 0.9 # Falls back to the owning Item. asset_extension . score = 0.7 assert asset . extra_fields [ "quality:score" ] == 0.7 assert extension . score == 0.9 asset_extension . validate () An Asset reads missing fields from its owning Item. An explicit asset value, including JSON null, takes precedence. Writes affect the Asset. Registration and full-schema validation use its owner, so attach assets before those operations. The same ownership requirement applies to Links and ItemAssetDefinitions. Only schema-discovered targets can be wrapped. Edit nested values ¶ extension . details = QualityDetails . create ( method = "automatic" , samples = 24 ) extension . details . method = "reviewed" assert item . properties [ "quality:details" ][ "method" ] == "reviewed" extension . validate () Nested wrappers expose create() , from_dict() , to_dict() , typed properties, and partial apply() . create() requires unconditionally required members, but full schema constraints are checked by the parent extension's validate() . Required nullable members may be supplied as None when the schema allows it. Nested property edits update the underlying JSON. Containers of wrappers are fresh views: after adding or removing list/map entries, assign the container back to its property. Assigning a nested object copies its serialized data; later changes to the original object do not change the assigned copy. Use a Collection summary helper ¶ From the repository checkout, generate the included View schema: pystac-ext-generator tests/fixtures/view.json -o view_extension.py from datetime import datetime , timezone import pystac from view_extension import ViewGeometryExtension collection = pystac . Collection ( id = "view-example" , description = "Images with viewing geometry" , extent = pystac . Extent ( pystac . SpatialExtent ([ - 180 , - 90 , 180 , 90 ]), pystac . TemporalExtent ([[ datetime ( 2026 , 1 , 1 , tzinfo = timezone . utc ), None ]]), ), ) summaries = ViewGeometryExtension . summaries ( collection , add_if_missing = True ) summaries . off_nadir = pystac . RangeSummary ( 0 , 30 ) assert summaries . off_nadir . maximum == 30 summaries . off_nadir = None Summary helpers are generated only for fields found under Collection summaries. They preserve lists, range summaries, and JSON Schema dictionaries, and do not aggregate Item values automatically. Top-level Collection fields use ext() when the schema declares that target; summary-only support does not imply it.

docs.text: Python API ¶ Use pystac_ext_generator when embedding generation in another Python tool: import json from pathlib import Path from pystac_ext_generator import generate schema = json . loads ( Path ( "quality-schema.json" ) . read_text ( encoding = "utf-8" )) source , warnings = generate ( schema , include_validation = True ) Path ( "quality_extension.py" ) . write_text ( source , encoding = "utf-8" ) for warning in warnings : print ( warning ) generate() returns source text and diagnostics. It checks the generated Python's syntax without executing it, then normalizes imports and formats the source with Ruff. prefix filters field namespaces. include_validation=True adds a standalone offline validator; its default is false. The full schema is retained whenever validation or nested union decoding requires it. Generation ¶ pystac_ext_generator . generate ( document : dict [ str , Any ], * , prefix : str | None = None , include_validation : bool = False , documents : Mapping [ str , dict [ str , Any ]] | None = None ) -> tuple [ str , list [ str ]] ¶ Return Python source and diagnostics. No generated code is executed. The schema title determines the extension class name and its canonical $id determines registration. Fields and applicable STAC objects are discovered from schema paths and references. Embedded offline validation is opt-in. Parameters: document ( dict [ str , Any ] ) – Full extension schema with a nonempty title and HTTP(S) $id. prefix ( str | None , default: None ) – Optional namespace filter, without the colon. documents ( Mapping [ str , dict [ str , Any ]] | None , default: None ) – Offline resources; missing external schemas are fetched over HTTP(S). include_validation ( bool , default: False ) – Embed the schema and a validate() method. Union decoding may require the schema even when this is false. Raises: SchemaError – If the schema, namespace, class name, or references cannot be supported. docs.text: CLI reference ¶ pystac-ext-generator [OPTIONS] SCHEMA SCHEMA is a JSON file path, HTTP(S) URL, or - for stdin. Option Behavior -o , --output FILE Write generated Python to a file; default is stdout. --prefix PREFIX Select a field namespace without its colon when multiple namespaces occur. --reference URI=FILE Supply an offline external schema mapping; repeat as needed. --resolve-external Fetch missing external HTTP(S) schema resources. --include-validation Embed the complete schema and an offline extension validate() method. --strict Treat generation warnings as errors. --force Permit overwriting the output file. --version Print the version from the package's shared version source. -h , --help Print usage information. Schema-derived settings ¶ Schema content Generated result title PascalCase class name, with Extension appended if absent. $id Canonical HTTP(S) registration URI; a trailing empty # is removed. Field placement and references Accessors at the applicable STAC object locations. Root properties.type.const or enum Object-type restrictions for the schema branch. Object properties, required members, and references Nested value classes and their factory parameters. For example, View Geometry Extension produces ViewGeometryExtension , and STAC Storage Extension produces STACStorageExtension . A title must contain ASCII letters or digits. Leading digits receive the prefix Value . Titles that collide with PySTAC base classes are rejected. The removed options --class-name , --schema-uri , --fields-pointer , and --target are not accepted. Their former Python API counterparts are also removed. Put that information in the full extension schema and update generated class imports when migrating from namespace-derived naming. Generated-code quality ¶ Ruff normalizes imports and formats generated source. The generator emits only needed conversions and schema-derived types. Its regression suite applies this repository's Ruff, strict mypy, and Bandit settings to generated files themselves. No generated-file lint, typing, or security suppressions are needed for the covered schemas. Default output omits full validation. Schema-dependent nested union decoding may still embed the schema and require jsonschema. Use --include-validation to opt into a public offline validator. Output and errors ¶ Generated Python is deterministic for the same schema and options. Output parent directories are created when needed. Existing files are preserved unless --force is given. Generation warnings and file-output notices go to stderr. Errors produce a nonzero exit status, including invalid schemas, missing external resources, unsupported reference scopes, and fields that cannot be discovered. The generator supports JSON Schema draft-07, 2019-09, and 2020-12. If $schema is absent, validation uses draft 2020-12. See limitations for unsupported constructs.

docs.text: Generated classes and fields ¶ Every generated module contains an extension class named from the schema title. Nested record schemas produce value classes, and summary fields produce a Summaries<ClassName> helper. No domain-specific extension classes are built in. Field naming and types ¶ The namespace is removed from Python attribute names: quality:score becomes score . JSON keys remain unchanged. Invalid identifier characters are normalized; Python keywords and wrapper-method collisions are escaped, such as class_ and apply_field . Remaining ambiguous names can cause a generation error. JSON Schema shape Python representation string , including date/time formats str ; format validation happens during schema validation. number , integer , boolean , null float , int , bool , None . Scalar enum or const Literal[...] where representable. Array with homogeneous items list[...] . Object with declared members Generated nested value class. Homogeneous additional-properties map dict[str, ...] , with typed values where supported. Open-ended object Raw dictionary. oneOf / anyOf Union annotations; nested codecs use schema validation to choose a representation. Absent extension fields return None . Setters preserve JSON values; annotations do not automatically coerce dates into datetime or enforce numeric bounds. The whole schema remains authoritative for validation. Extension operations ¶ Operation Contract Extension.ext(obj, add_if_missing=False) Wrap a supported target and check extension membership; optionally register it. get_schema_uri() Return the canonical registration URI. has_extension() , add_to() , remove_from() Manage the exact schema version on a STAC object. Typed properties Read or write fields at the appropriate storage location. apply(**values) Update supplied Python field names; precheck unknown/inapplicable names. clear(name) Remove a field by its Python name. set_null(name) Store explicit JSON null; schema validation determines whether it is allowed. validate() (opt-in) With --include-validation , validate the wrapped object or its owner against the embedded schema. summaries(collection, add_if_missing=False) Wrap Collection summaries when supported by the schema. Items store fields in properties ; Collections, Catalogs, Assets, and Links use extra_fields ; ItemAssetDefinitions use properties . Assets fall back to Item properties for missing values. Summary helpers preserve lists, ranges, and schema objects. They expose field properties, rather than an extension-style apply() . Nested value classes ¶ Nested classes provide create() , from_dict(properties, copy=False) , to_dict() , typed properties, apply() , clear() , and set_null() . Required factory arguments come from unconditional requirements, including merged allOf object fields. create() preserves explicit None ; setters and apply() remove fields assigned None . Unknown JSON properties survive round-trips. Class names use reference names when meaningful, otherwise field naming hints. Collisions receive numeric suffixes, equivalent shapes may share a class, and recursive records use forward annotations. See mutation semantics for live views versus copied assignments. Large nested classes use schema-generated TypedDict keyword declarations with Unpack for create() and apply() . These preserve named argument typing and required members without oversized function signatures. Runtime checks still reject unknown keywords and missing required values before mutation. Module metadata ¶ SCHEMA (conditional): the original or bundled schema, emitted for optional offline validation or schema-dependent union decoding. SCHEMA_URI : canonical registration identifier. FIELD_NAMES : Python attribute names mapped to JSON keys. FIELD_TARGETS : JSON keys mapped to their discovered targets. TARGETS : the module's combined applicability.

docs.text: Generate your first extension ¶ Install the CLI , then work in an empty directory. This example defines a small quality-metadata extension for Items and their Assets. 1. Save the extension schema ¶ Save the following as quality-schema.json : { "$schema" : "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema" , "$id" : "https://example.org/quality/v1.0.0/schema.json" , "title" : "Quality Extension" , "type" : "object" , "required" : [ "type" , "stac_extensions" , "properties" ], "properties" : { "type" : { "const" : "Feature" }, "stac_extensions" : { "type" : "array" , "contains" : { "const" : "https://example.org/quality/v1.0.0/schema.json" } }, "properties" : { "$ref" : "#/$defs/fields" }, "assets" : { "type" : "object" , "additionalProperties" : { "$ref" : "#/$defs/fields" } } }, "$defs" : { "fields" : { "type" : "object" , "properties" : { "quality:score" : { "description" : "Quality score between zero and one." , "type" : "number" , "minimum" : 0 , "maximum" : 1 }, "quality:details" : { "$ref" : "#/$defs/quality_details" } } }, "quality_details" : { "type" : "object" , "required" : [ "method" ], "properties" : { "method" : { "type" : "string" }, "samples" : { "type" : "integer" , "minimum" : 1 } } } } } The example.org identifier is illustrative. This tutorial validates against the schema embedded in the generated module, so that URL does not need to resolve. Use a published canonical schema URL for an extension you distribute. 2. Generate the Python module ¶ pystac-ext-generator quality-schema.json --include-validation -o quality_extension.py This tutorial opts into embedded validation so its illustrative schema can be validated offline. Without --include-validation , use PySTAC item.validate() and a published or locally configured schema resolver. The title produces QualityExtension , and the referenced object definition produces QualityDetails . The references under Item properties and assets establish applicability automatically. Existing output files are protected; pass --force when regenerating intentionally. 3. Use the generated classes ¶ Save this as use_quality.py next to the generated module: import json from datetime import datetime , timezone import pystac from quality_extension import QualityDetails , QualityExtension item = pystac . Item ( id = "quality-example" , geometry = None , bbox = None , datetime = datetime ( 2026 , 1 , 1 , tzinfo = timezone . utc ), properties = {}, ) extension = QualityExtension . ext ( item , add_if_missing = True ) extension . apply ( score = 0.9 , details = QualityDetails . create ( method = "manual" , samples = 12 ), ) extension . validate () serialized = json . loads ( json . dumps ( item . to_dict ())) assert serialized [ "properties" ][ "quality:score" ] == 0.9 assert QualityExtension . get_schema_uri () in serialized [ "stac_extensions" ] restored_item = pystac . Item . from_dict ( serialized ) restored = QualityExtension . ext ( restored_item ) assert restored . details . method == "manual" assert restored . details . samples == 12 restored . validate () Run it: python use_quality.py add_if_missing=True registers the schema URI on the Item. Nested value classes serialize as ordinary JSON objects. validate() checks the whole Item against the embedded extension schema; to_dict() alone does not validate values. Continue with updates, asset inheritance, and nested values .

docs.text: Install the CLI , then work in an empty directory. This example defines a small quality-metadata extension for Items and their Assets.
docs.title: Generate your first extension

docs.text: Save the following as quality-schema.json : { "$schema" : "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema" , "$id" : "https://example.org/quality/v1.0.0/schema.json" , "title" : "Quality Extension" , "type" : "object" , "required" : [ "type" , "stac_extensions" , "properties" ], "properties" : { "type" : { "const" : "Feature" }, "stac_extensions" : { "type" : "array" , "contains" : { "const" : "https://example.org/quality/v1.0.0/schema.json" } }, "properties" : { "$ref" : "#/$defs/fields" }, "assets" : { "type" : "object" , "additionalProperties" : { "$ref" : "#/$defs/fields" } } }, "$defs" : { "fields" : { "type" : "object" , "properties" : { "quality:score" : { "description" : "Quality score between zero and one." , "type" : "number" , "minimum" : 0 , "maximum" : 1 }, "quality:details" : { "$ref" : "#/$defs/quality_details" } } }, "quality_details" : { "type" : "object" , "required" : [ "method" ], "properties" : { "method" : { "type" : "string" }, "samples" : { "type" : "integer" , "minimum" : 1 } } } } } The example.org identifier is illustrative. This tutorial validates against the schema embedded in the generated module, so that URL does not need to resolve. Use a published canonical schema URL for an extension you distribute.
docs.title: 1. Save the extension schema

docs.text: pystac-ext-generator quality-schema.json --include-validation -o quality_extension.py This tutorial opts into embedded validation so its illustrative schema can be validated offline. Without --include-validation , use PySTAC item.validate() and a published or locally configured schema resolver. The title produces QualityExtension , and the referenced object definition produces QualityDetails . The references under Item properties and assets establish applicability automatically. Existing output files are protected; pass --force when regenerating intentionally.
docs.title: 2. Generate the Python module

docs.text: Save this as use_quality.py next to the generated module: import json from datetime import datetime , timezone import pystac from quality_extension import QualityDetails , QualityExtension item = pystac . Item ( id = "quality-example" , geometry = None , bbox = None , datetime = datetime ( 2026 , 1 , 1 , tzinfo = timezone . utc ), properties = {}, ) extension = QualityExtension . ext ( item , add_if_missing = True ) extension . apply ( score = 0.9 , details = QualityDetails . create ( method = "manual" , samples = 12 ), ) extension . validate () serialized = json . loads ( json . dumps ( item . to_dict ())) assert serialized [ "properties" ][ "quality:score" ] == 0.9 assert QualityExtension . get_schema_uri () in serialized [ "stac_extensions" ] restored_item = pystac . Item . from_dict ( serialized ) restored = QualityExtension . ext ( restored_item ) assert restored . details . method == "manual" assert restored . details . samples == 12 restored . validate () Run it: python use_quality.py add_if_missing=True registers the schema URI on the Item. Nested value classes serialize as ordinary JSON objects. validate() checks the whole Item against the embedded extension schema; to_dict() alone does not validate values. Continue with updates, asset inheritance, and nested values .
